local_comparison: On kuṭa kauṭilye the kuṭādi rule 1.2.1 already gives ṅit treatment to aru in this environment.
1.1.5 blocks ordinary guṇa under that treatment. Explicit k cannot be distinguished there by comparing the two outcomes.

traditional_resolution.argument: The renewed prescription of kit indicates non-invariability of inherited ṅit treatment. In another environment guṇa occurs.
The kuṭ operation already succeeds under ṅit. His verse presents the explicit k as indicating guṇa elsewhere, naming koṭara and koṭīra among the examples.

questions.status: traditional explanatory function attested in these two commentaries
questions.boundary: The external function is a jñāpaka on these analyses. Extend guṇa only under independent licensing for a particular lexical path. Ujjvaladatta leaves the purpose open.

questions.primary: kliś + kan, prescribed long ī, deletion of l and insertion of nām

traditional_readings.policy: Specifies kliś in the sense vibādhane. Leaves the effect of k undecided.

Both entries allowed because the rule states no distinguishing qualifier. Gives Yama, quotes Māgha, and calls k a marker for the work of kit. The next explicit function is ascribed to m: 1.1.47 places nām after the last vowel.
Gives the prescribed ī, l loss and the insertion associated with nām, leading to the Yama reading. The explanation identifies no independent differential effect for k.

questions.status: specific grammatical effect of k remains open
questions.boundary: The explicit m placement must not be assigned to k. The broader root inventory belongs to Śvetavanavāsin alone.

construction: Carry root-entry ID, the affix marker, prior ṅit designation, local operation, the named other environments and the witness as separate fields. Projecting only kuṭaru loses the distinction between a local prohibition and a cross-rule inference.
